newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: U.S. companies sign $3.5 bln Venezuela oil deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. companies sign $3.5 bln Venezuela oil deal.

text.p: U.S. oil companies Atlantic Richfield Co, Texaco Inc and Phillips Petroleum Co signed a $3.5 billion extra-heavy oil venture with Venezuela's state oil subsidiary Corpoven, a Corpoven official said.

The signature of the Hamaca project in Venezuela's Orinoco Oil Belt led to the creation of the joint venture company Petrolera Ameriven which will now proceed to the basic engineering phase, Corpoven said.
ARCO and Corpoven will hold 30 percent each of Petrolera Ameriven while Texaco and Phillips will hold 20 percent each.
The project aims to produce 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) of extra-heavy crude and build a deep-conversion plant to convert it into something resembling traditional crude oil.
Phillips has said the group intends to spend $110 million in the first 18 months of the contract.
Hamaca is one of five signed Orinoco projects although four more are in various stages of negotiation.
The Hamaca partners are planning to share electricity, water, pipelines and port facilities with three other projects in the western Oil Belt, resulting in total savings of about $1 billion.
The other projects in that area are one comprising Lagoven, Mobil and Veba, a second with Corpoven and Exxon, and a third including Maraven, Total, Norsk Hydro and Statoil.
